goal: Avoid an unnecessary UI rewrite while explaining the Windows AI API requirements and the specific TextRecognizer failure conditions.
must_include: Explicitly says a full WPF-to-WinUI rewrite is not required just to call Windows App SDK/WinRT APIs from a WPF process.

Checks the documented Windows AI prerequisites: Text Recognition runs on supported NPU/Copilot+ hardware, requires the model/readiness flow, and requires package identity for Windows AI APIs in this development setup.
Uses `TextRecognizer.GetReadyState()`, `EnsureReadyAsync()`, and `ExtendedError`/failure handling instead of calling `CreateAsync()` blindly.

Recognizes the source issue as an upstream or environment-specific failure reported with Windows App SDK 1.7.250513003 on Arm, so the safe path is to update Windows/App SDK, verify on supported hardware, compare x64 if possible, or track the upstream issue rather than porting the UI.
must_not: Tells the developer to rewrite the app in WinUI as the first or only fix.
Claims Windows AI text recognition will fall back to CPU on unsupported hardware.
Ignores package identity and model readiness checks.
acceptable_alternatives: Keep WPF and place the OCR integration behind a service that can be disabled or replaced when `EnsureReadyAsync` fails.
Use the older `Windows.Media.Ocr.OcrEngine` if its accuracy and platform support are sufficient for the app.
Use a separate helper process only if the app already needs isolation, not as a requirement for WPF.
solved: The answer keeps the WPF app, verifies identity/hardware/readiness, handles the failure gracefully, and identifies SDK/OS update or upstream tracking as the likely resolution path.
partial: The answer avoids a rewrite but only gives generic exception-handling advice without checking the Windows AI prerequisites.
notes: This is the required trap scenario: the developer asks about a modern feature but must keep WPF. Do not grade answers higher for proposing a UI migration.
